paragraphs.source_en: “In those days I was famous as a champion eater of strange things, and I had grown tired of locusts, slugs, toads, and the like. Snake rice, however, was something novel, so I told the old man that it sounded splendid and that I would gladly impose on them. Thereupon the old man set a pot over the hearth, put in rice, and began to simmer it. The odd thing was that the lid of the pot had about ten holes in it, large and small. Steam kept puffing up through those holes. I thought to myself, what an ingenious contrivance; for country folk, this was really admirable. Just then the old man suddenly stood up and went off somewhere. After a while he came back carrying a large basket under his arm and set it casually beside the hearth. When I looked inside, well, there were plenty of them: long creatures, crowded together one by one, coiled around one another.”
